statement: A California employment invention-assignment agreement cannot reach an invention the employee developed entirely on their own time without using the employer's equipment, supplies, facilities, or trade secret information, unless the invention relates to the employer's business or actual or demonstrably anticipated research or development, or results from work performed for the employer; a contrary provision is unenforceable (Labor Code § 2870(a)-(b)).
caveat: Labor Code § 2872 requires the agreement to notify the employee of § 2870's limits for the assignment to be enforceable against inventions the section protects. Similar statutes exist in WA, DE, and other states. This repo does not review specific agreements.
